key_insight: Rarefied hypersonic surface loads over triangular protrusions are nonlocal, but the “information length” depends on the quantity: heat transfer shows the strongest bulk-to-wall influence, pressure is often captured within a few protrusion lengths, and shear is the least identifiable.
engineering_relevance: For hypersonic vehicle design, this means wall-load prediction and surrogate modeling must account for quantity-specific nonlocal physics rather than relying on a single near-wall neighborhood size.
method: DSMC simulations over Mach 4–8, Kn 0.1–0.8, and three protrusion orientations
Circular bulk neighborhoods summarized with weighted statistics, extrema, nearest-point values, and tangent-normal gradients of velocity, temperature, and pressure
Region-to-point diagnostics for Cp, Cq, and |τ| with R95 used to identify the minimum radius matching full-domain error behavior
evidence_signal: Using full-domain descriptors reduced wall-profile error from 45.5% to 13.8% for Cp, from 72.6% to 12.9% for Cq, and from 49.1% to 31.9% for shear, with heat transfer showing the clearest order-hs nonlocal support.
watch_item: The surrogate gains are only partially preserved in closed-loop audits, with the largest degradation appearing for forward-facing heat transfer and shear.
paper_title: Quantity-Dependent Bulk-to-Wall Observability of Surface Loading in Rarefied Hypersonic Flow over Triangular Protrusions
